title: Shivram Singh v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam
coram: Surya Prakash Kesarwani, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner left to object under para 8.1 of the 2005 Code.
headnote: A writ seeking to quash a final assessment notice for alleged electricity theft is not the proper course. The consumer must submit an objection before the concerned authority under paragraph 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Division Bench disposed of the petition without any opinion on merits, leaving that objection open before respondent No. 2.
facts: Shivram Singh filed Writ-C No. 33219 of 2021 in the Allahabad High Court against Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam and another, praying to quash a final assessment notice issued on account of alleged electricity theft. Counsel for the petitioner and for the respondents were heard. The consumer invoked the writ jurisdiction at the notice stage of the theft assessment, instead of first placing an objection before the assessing authority impleaded as respondent No. 2.

holding_units.topic: theft assessment notice — writ versus clause 8.1 objection
holding_units.holding: The proper course for a consumer seeking to challenge a final assessment notice issued on alleged electricity theft is to submit an objection before the concerned authority in accordance with law under paragraph 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ petition is disposed of without any opinion on merits, leaving that objection open before respondent No. 2.

principle_tags.application: The Court would not quash a theft-related final assessment notice on the writ side and relegated the consumer to the paragraph 8.1 objection before the assessing authority.

not_decided.point: Merits of the theft final assessment notice
not_decided.note: The Court expressly declined to express any opinion on the merits of the petitioner's case.
